bandReport.notes: Band b2 = p07-p12, Q58-Q100 complete (43 items). SEAM BEFORE: p06 (band b1's territory) ends cleanly at Q57 with all four options printed; no Directions block is open across the p06/p07 boundary, so Q58 starts clean. SEAM AFTER: none - p12 is the LAST page of the booklet and the paper genuinely ENDS AT Q100. Verified at 3x zoom that the final printed line of p12 is Q100's option (d) 'sufficient data' (the wrapped tail of 'Cannot be determined due to insufficient data'); nothing follows it. NO ANSWER KEY appears anywhere on p07-p12 - no key page, no key table, no marginal answers. EIGHT Directions sets, ALL of which START inside this band, so this band owns every member of every one: D76-78 (cone-on-hemisphere solid, block starts p09), D79-80 (chord subtending 120 deg, block starts p09 RIGHT column, Q79 on p09 and Q80 overleaf on p10), D81-83 (triangle 6-10-8 with three mutually touching circles, p10), D84-85 (isosceles ABC with D on BC, p10), D86-88 (triangle 1.6-6.3-6.5 with mid-points P and Q, block starts p10 RIGHT column, Q86-Q87 on p10 and Q88 overleaf on p11), D89-90 (AB diameter, OP perpendicular to AB, p11), D91-94 (two pie charts 2019/2020, p11), D95-98 (grouped bar chart of car production 2014-2018, p12), D99-100 (five consecutive integers, p12). Two of those sets straddle a page break INSIDE the band (D79-80 and D86-88); both are transcribed whole here. TWO FIGURES, both data-interpretation and both SHARED across a whole set: the pie-chart pair (Q91-Q94) and the bar chart (Q95-Q98). NO geometry item in this band carries a printed figure - Q89/Q90 and every other geometry stem states its configuration entirely in words, which matches the sibling-paper finding that some CDS Maths papers ship no geometry diagrams at all.

The minute hand of a clock is 21 cm long. What is the area on the face of the clock described by the minute hand between 10.10 a.m and 10.30 a.m ? (take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))
flags: The booklet prints the two clock times with its raised middle dot (as '10<middot>10 a.m' and '10<middot>30 a.m'). Here that dot is a TIME separator, not a decimal point; rendered as a full stop per the brief's glyph rule, so 10.10 a.m means ten minutes past ten. Also printed 'a.m' with no trailing full stop - transcribed as printed.

The following Pie-Charts show the percentage of different categories (\(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\), \(E\) and \(F\)) of employees in a company in the year 2019 and 2020. The total number of employees was 4000 in 2019 and 5000 in 2020.
questions.figureNote: p11, LEFT column: the shared stimulus of the Q91-Q94 set - TWO pie charts side by side, running from just below the line 'and 5000 in 2020.' down to and INCLUDING the two boxed year captions '2019' and '2020' printed beneath them. Crop both charts as ONE image. Each circle is divided by solid radii into six sectors; the percentage sits INSIDE the sector and the category letter (A, B, C, D, E, F) sits OUTSIDE the circle, some of them at the far left/right edge of the column, so crop the full column width with a margin on all four sides rather than tightening to the circles. Printed values, for verification of the crop: 2019 chart - A 20%, B 6%, C 10%, D 15%, E 27%, F 22% (sums to 100); 2020 chart - A 22%, B 10%, C 11%, D 9%, E 27%, F 21% (sums to 100). These percentages plus the two year captions are the entire data of all four questions; clipping any one sector label or either year box makes the set unanswerable.
